sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 of the September 1928 Sanborn atlas of Runnemede, Camden County, New Jersey. The upper half of the page carries the title cartouche, the key, the water and fire department notes, the street and specials index and a key map of the borough at about 800 feet to an inch; this reading covers only the lower half, the map proper, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the left of the page. It shows the eastern edge of the borough around Clements Bridge Road, which runs diagonally down the left side with a 10-inch water pipe in it. East of the road lie the blocks between Forest Avenue at the top of the page and Schubert Avenue at the bottom, crossed by Oak and Pine Avenues and by Highland Avenue and Davis Road, which run across the page. A short diagonal Forest Avenue leaves Clements Bridge Road to join the main Forest Avenue near Highland Avenue. Parts of Forest and Oak Avenues are marked not open, and 3rd Avenue at the bottom left is also marked not open. The area is a thinly built residential subdivision: most lots are empty and the buildings are scattered frame dwellings with a few outbuildings, all colored yellow. Large block numbers (283 to 293, 400) fill the unbuilt ground. The right edge of the map is marked no exposure, and a dash-dot match line lettered A and B runs along the bottom edge toward sheet 3.
notes: Only the lower half of the sheet is georeferenced; the key map in the upper half (about 800 ft to an inch) is masked out.
Highland Avenue on this sheet is today Stratford Avenue; Forest Avenue is spelled Forrest Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The line work on this sheet is fainter than on the others; the detector needed a lower ink threshold (30).

Map, 100 ft. Top half is the title block, key map (800 ft to an inch), key and street index (not configured, masked out); lower half is map sheet 1: Clements Bridge Road east of Hill Av, Forest, Oak, Pine, Schubert Avs, Highland Av, Davis Rd. Drawn with north to the left. One part.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the September 1928 Sanborn atlas of Runnemede, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. It covers the centre of the borough on both sides of Black Horse Pike, which runs down the middle of the page, and the Atlantic City Railroad (P. and R. Ry., Gloucester and Mt. Ephraim Branch) just west of it, with the Runnemede station beside the track. Clements Bridge Road crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right. North of it are 1st and 2nd Avenues with Oakland, Bowers and Railroad Avenues on the west and Central Avenue on the east; the Runnemede Fire Co. No. 1 house stands on the Pike near 1st Avenue, with a cluster of stores and dwellings. South of Clements Bridge Road the east side is a newer subdivision: St. Claire Road, Plaza Place, Haverford Road and Ardmore Avenue between the Pike and Central and Lindsay Avenues, with Knight Avenue at the upper right. St. Teresa Catholic Church stands on Ardmore Avenue. The west side holds Oakland, Pineland and Phillips Avenues, Shisler Circle, and Charles, Elmer and Walter Avenues, largely vacant lots. Evesham Road and the borough limits with Gloucester Township run along the bottom edge. A small stream crosses the blocks between Oakland and Bowers Avenues. Hydrants are noted as not in service at the time of survey, and 6-inch water pipes are drawn in several streets. Most buildings are frame dwellings colored yellow.
notes: Renamed since: Lindsay Avenue is Lindsey Avenue; St. Claire Road is Saint Clair Road; Pineland Avenue is South Read Avenue; Central Avenue south of Lindsay Avenue is Washington Avenue; Oakland Avenue south of Clements Bridge Road is South Oakland Avenue.
Plaza Place and Black Horse Pike at Ardmore Avenue disagree with their modern positions by about 7 to 15 m relative to the rest of the sheet; Plaza Place was left out of the control.
Station: Runnemede, Atlantic City R.R. Fire house: Runnemede Fire Co. No. 1.

Map, 100 ft. Centre of town: Black Horse Pike and the Atlantic City R.R. (P&R Ry), Clements Bridge Rd, 1st/2nd Av, Central, Lindsay, Knight, St Claire, Plaza Pl, Haverford, Ardmore, Oakland, Bowers, Pineland, Phillips, Charles, Elmer, Walter, Shisler Circle, Evesham Rd. North up. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 of the September 1928 Sanborn atlas of Runnemede, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. It covers the eastern part of the borough between Central Avenue on the left and the borough's eastern blocks, with Clements Bridge Road running diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. North of the road the grid of numbered avenues (1st to 5th) runs east from Central Avenue, with Gravel Hill Road cutting diagonally across the top left, a short 7th Avenue, and Link Avenue, 3rd and 4th Avenues and Irish Hill Road farther east. The Runnemede School, a brick building, stands on Central Avenue between 2nd and 3rd Avenues, with the Mt. Calvary Union Church nearby on 2nd Avenue. Beside Clements Bridge Road at Irish Hill Road stands the Irish Hill Concrete Products Co., with its block and mixing sheds. South of the road a long subdivision of narrow lots lies between Lindsay, Knight, Johnson, Harding, Mitchell and Hill Avenues, laid out diagonally; Trinity Lutheran Church stands at Knight Avenue near Clements Bridge Road. Most of these lots are still empty and the eastern third of the sheet (block 23) is open ground marked no exposure, with a hydrant note saying hydrants were not in service at the time of survey. Plaza Place and Central Avenue appear at the bottom left. Buildings are mostly frame dwellings; 10-inch and 6-inch water pipes are drawn in Clements Bridge Road and Lindsay and Knight Avenues.
notes: Renamed since: 5th Avenue east of Gravel Hill Road is Union Avenue; Link Avenue and the diagonal 4th Avenue segment are now part of Hill Avenue; Lindsay Avenue is Lindsey Avenue; Central Avenue at the bottom left (south of Lindsay) is Washington Avenue.
Buildings of note: Runnemede School, Mt. Calvary Union Church, Trinity Lutheran Church, Irish Hill Concrete Products Co.

Map, 100 ft. East of Central Av: 1st to 5th Avs, Gravel Hill Rd, Link Av, Irish Hill Rd, Clements Bridge Rd, Hill, Mitchell, Harding, Johnson, Knight, Lindsay Avs; Runnemede School, Irish Hill Concrete Products Co. North up. One part.

sheet-4-1.description: Main map of sheet 4 of the September 1928 Sanborn atlas of Runnemede, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. It occupies the whole sheet except the boxed inset at the top left and covers the western part of the borough along Clements Bridge Road, which crosses the lower half of the page from the left edge toward the upper right. In the upper right are Read, Pineland and Oakland Avenues running down from 1st Avenue to Clements Bridge Road, with a small stream crossing the blocks; Read Avenue is marked not open in part. The lower part shows Sheppard Avenue (not open) at the top left and, south of Clements Bridge Road, Rowand, Highland and Woodland Avenues running down to Evesham Road, the borough limits with Gloucester Township along the bottom edge. Phillips Avenue and the curve of Shisler Circle lie at the lower right, with Walter Avenue and the ends of Charles and Elmer Avenues at the right edge. A second branch of the stream runs south across the blocks east of Woodland Avenue. Development is scattered: frame dwellings, colored yellow, with a few small outbuildings and a store or two along Clements Bridge Road, and large blocks of empty lots. Block numbers 245 to 263 and 18 to 21 identify the blocks. The scale bar is at the bottom left.
notes: Renamed since: Pineland Avenue is South Read Avenue; Read Avenue is North Read Avenue; Rowand, Highland and Woodland Avenues are North and South Rowand, North and South Highland and South Woodland Avenues.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 the main map (Clements Bridge Rd west of the railroad: Rowand, Highland, Woodland, Oakland, Pineland/Read, Phillips, Shisler Circle, Sheppard); part 2 the boxed inset at top left (Clements Bridge Rd at Big Timber Creek: Singley, Bassett, Holly, Rowand, Sheppard, Woodland), drawn west of part 1.

sheet-4-2.description: Inset in a heavy-ruled box at the top left of sheet 4 of the September 1928 Sanborn atlas of Runnemede, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. It shows the western end of the borough along Clements Bridge Road from Big Timber Creek, which winds down the left side of the box and forms the boundary with Deptford Township, east toward Rowand Avenue. The inset lies directly west of the main map of the sheet, which continues the same streets beyond Rowand Avenue. North of the road are Bassett, Singley and Holly Avenues running up to Sheppard Avenue, which is marked not open in part, with Rowand Avenue along the right side of the box and a short Woodland Avenue at the top left. South of the road the strip of lots runs down to Evesham Road and the borough limits with Gloucester Township along the bottom of the box. Buildings are frame dwellings, colored yellow, closely spaced near the creek between Bassett and Singley Avenues, with an inn, a garage and several stores along Clements Bridge Road. Block numbers 231 to 262 identify the blocks. The creek is drawn in blue with the township line along it.
notes: Rowand Avenue is today North Rowand Avenue.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 the main map (Clements Bridge Rd west of the railroad: Rowand, Highland, Woodland, Oakland, Pineland/Read, Phillips, Shisler Circle, Sheppard); part 2 the boxed inset at top left (Clements Bridge Rd at Big Timber Creek: Singley, Bassett, Holly, Rowand, Sheppard, Woodland), drawn west of part 1.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 of the September 1928 Sanborn atlas of Runnemede, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. It covers the northern part of the borough between 1st Avenue at the bottom and Smiths Lane near the top. Black Horse Pike runs down the right third of the page, and the Atlantic City Railroad (Gloucester and Mt. Ephraim Branch) runs down the middle with Railroad Avenue beside it. West of the railroad, Read, Oakland and Bowers Avenues run up the page, continuing north of 5th Avenue as 4th, 3rd and W. 2nd Avenues to Smiths Lane, and are crossed by 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 5th Avenues; these blocks are closely built with rows of frame dwellings. Between the railroad and the Pike the blocks along 7th, 6th, 5th, 4th and 2nd Avenues hold uniform rows of houses, many of them brick (colored pink), with a large lot (block 193A) between 4th and 2nd Avenues. East of the Pike are the ends of 2nd to 6th Avenues, with Gravel Hill Road running diagonally from the Pike at the upper right; its upper part is marked not open. The streets north of Smiths Lane (5th Avenue, 1st Avenue, E. 2nd Avenue) belong to sheet 6. Block numbers 15 and 190 to 209 and 379 to 386 identify the blocks.
notes: Renamed since: Smiths Lane is Smith Lane; Read, Oakland and Bowers Avenues (with their northern parts printed 4th, 3rd and W. 2nd Avenues) are North Read, North Oakland and Bowers Avenues; the numbered avenues are West or East 1st to 7th Avenue on either side of Black Horse Pike.
Map, 100 ft. North of 1st Av: Read, Oakland, Bowers Avs, W. 2nd Av, the railroad, Black Horse Pike, 1st to 7th Avs, Smiths Lane, Gravel Hill Rd. North up. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 of the September 1928 Sanborn atlas of Runnemede, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with north to the left. It covers the north end of the borough beyond Smiths Lane, which runs down the right side. Black Horse Pike runs along the top edge, with the Runnemede Theatre (a vaudeville and moving picture house, brick) at the upper right and the Marland Club on 1st Avenue. Broadway, New Jersey Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue run down the page from the Pike, and are crossed by numbered avenues running parallel to the Pike: 1st, W. 2nd and E. 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th Avenues, with Rose Avenue at the upper left. The Atlantic City Railroad (Gloucester and Mt. Ephraim Branch) crosses the sheet diagonally beside 2nd Avenue. Most of the ground west of Broadway is laid out in lots but unbuilt, and several avenues are marked not open; the built-up part is the strip east of Broadway, with rows of frame dwellings and a group of brick houses on 6th Avenue. Beaver Branch and the boundary with the Borough of Bellmawr cross the upper left corner. Block numbers 160 to 189 identify the blocks. The numbered avenues here repeat the names used south of Smiths Lane, as the index notes.
notes: The numbered avenues north of Smiths Lane are renamed: 1st Avenue is Elm Avenue, W. 2nd Avenue is Bowers Avenue, 3rd Avenue is North Oakland Avenue, 4th Avenue is North Read Avenue, 5th Avenue is Orchard Avenue, 6th Avenue is Rambler Avenue (identified from the spacing along Broadway and Smith Lane). Smiths Lane is Smith Lane.
Pennsylvania Avenue and the western blocks are crossed today by the New Jersey Turnpike; New Jersey Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue were not used for control.
Buildings of note: Runnemede Theatre, the Marland Club.

Map, 100 ft. North of Smiths Lane: Black Horse Pike, New Jersey Av, Broadway, Pennsylvania Av, Rose Av, 1st to 7th Avs (numbered again north of Smiths Lane), Gloucester and Mt Ephraim Branch railroad, Beaver Branch. Drawn turned, north to the left. One part.
